clauses.reason: lead: The lead paragraph recites the authority (Title II of the act of November 26, 1940), the Civil Service Commission recommendation and the finding that the action is necessary, and introduces the two numbered items. It commands nothing itself and is exhausted when the items it introduces are performed, on 1943-03-15, the date item 2 gives.

item 1: Executive Order No. 8955 of December 1, 1941 is "is hereby" revoked (the verb phrase and 'revoked' are printed on two lines). Item 2 makes the order take effect as of March 15, 1943, so the one-time revocation was performed as of that date; the order is exhausted by performance and EO 8955 stays revoked as a surviving consequence.

item 2: "This order shall take effect as of" March 15, 1943 (the date is printed on the next line). The item fixes the effective date of item 1; it is performed on that date and leaves no continuing duty.

research_rationale:
EO 9314 (signed March 15, 1943; F.R. Doc. 43-4093, filed March 16, 1943) was read in full in the registered held text (machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF, grade original_representation_unverified, under jobs/fr-originals); the heading, body, signature, date and filing line were read; page images were not compared. Under Title II of the act of November 26, 1940, on the recommendation of the Civil Service Commission, it revokes EO 8955 of December 1, 1941 (which extended the Classification Act of 1923 to certain War and Navy Department positions and set a salary differential) and provides that the order takes effect as of March 15, 1943. The held text continues with a Civil Service Commission regulation after the filing line; that is another document and was not used. All three scopes are performed together on 1943-03-15 and are exhausted by performance; the revocation of EO 8955 stays in place as a surviving consequence. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.

savings.reason: The order states no savings clause. Because the revocation of EO 8955 takes effect as of March 15, 1943, acts and payments made under EO 8955 before that date are accrued effects the revocation did not undo; nothing continues as a command under EO 9314.
